messages:
Rachel (sec): Heads-up: we're rolling RBAC changes next week that expand 'grant' and 'revoke' events. Need quick sync on audit schema, customer validation surface, and the ingestion cost/throughput impact. worried about explosion of high-volume events from automated role syncs.
Alex M: +1. Two immediate asks: define minimal required fields for every audit event; and a plan for high-volume clients (sampling, batching).
Priya S: For RBAC we need `actor`, `target_type`, `target_id`, `action`, `scope`, `request_id`, `timestamp`, and `tenant_id` as required. Also include `policy_version` for future debugging.
Marco (ingest): If we mandate tenant_id and request_id we can shard and dedupe upstream which helps indexing. Big concern: per-event envelope encryption with KMS per tenant will spike KMS calls.
SRE-Tim: On ingest/backpressure: implement per-tenant token buckets + global circuit breaker. When queue > 85% start shedding non-critical events (audit sampling) and emit metrics.
Rachel (sec): Customer-facing: we must surface validation errors so integrators know why events were dropped. Prefer returning 202 + event_id + validation_status (valid|invalid) with `failure_reason` when invalid. Don’t return actual PII in error text.
Compliance-Anna: Also provide a validation endpoint (dry-run) customers can call to check schema before sending bulk loads. Must be opt-in for privacy.
Alex M: Implementation notes: for validation we can do synchronous lightweight schema check on receive and enqueue async deep validation. Response: `{"event_id":"<uuid>","validation_status":"accepted_pending_full_check"}` for most.
Marco (ingest): For KMS costs: propose DEK caching per worker with TTL + encrypt DEK under tenant KEK via KMS on rotation only. That reduces KMS call cardinality from events -> rotations. Also batch envelope encryption for bulk writes.
Priya S: Is DEK caching acceptable from security? Need threat model: cached DEKs are in process memory only, rotated on rotation window and on restart. Add HSM/KMS usage logs.
Rachel (sec): OK but add guardrails: in-memory DEKs with strict TTL (e.g., 10m), memory zeroing on GC if possible, and require allowlist for any team that enables DEK cache. Document in audit policy.
SRE-Tim: Indexing cost: change ES mapping to use keyword for `action` and compressed doc_values for tenant_id to reduce cost. Also switch bulk size heuristic: 1MB compressed or 5000 docs, whichever first.
Alex M: For schema migration we should use a feature-flagged write path: accept v1 and v2 concurrently, enrich v1 to v2 where possible, and ship a reindex job run during low-cost window. Canary 1% of traffic to new mapping first.
Marco (ingest): For throughput we’ll also enable prefix/KV cache for repeated large events (e.g., automated syncs) so we can avoid reindexing identical payloads; add `event_fingerprint` hashed from stable fields for dedupe.
Compliance-Anna: Customer docs: detail required fields, sample curl/gzip bulk ingest, and a `validation-test` endpoint with examples and expected responses. Also include SLA note on validation latency.
Priya S: Vulnerability triage: ensure any validation code runs in sandboxed path and library dependencies are audited. Add unit tests for malformed payloads and fuzz harness.
Rachel (sec): Incident playbook: if ingestion backlog grows > 30m for critical tenants, auto-open incident, throttle non-critical tenants, and engage customers via status page.
SRE-Tim: Metrics to add: per-tenant ingest rate, queue length, KMS call rate, DEK cache hit rate, validation_failure_rate, and percentage of events sampled/dropped. Dashboards and alerting thresholds doc to follow.
Alex M: Quick dev tasks: (1) schema PR (v2) with example event, (2) validation endpoint stub, (3) DEK cache prototype, (4) backpressure circuit breaker + sampling policy. I'll pick up 1 & 4.
Marco (ingest): I'll prototype DEK cache and change bulk writer to accept batched encryption. Will run load test with synthetic RBAC bursts.
Priya S: I'll add policy doc for required fields and RBAC audit log semantics. Also will review threat model for DEK caching.
Compliance-Anna: I'll draft customer-facing validation docs and the dry-run contract.
Rachel (sec): Great. Can everyone drop short PR links in this thread when ready. If heavy rollout, we'll schedule a 30min sync Wed.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: New canary pipeline created: `audit-schema-v2-canary` — triggered when PR linked. :rocket:
Alex M: :+1: thanks everyone.
SRE-Tim: filing a tracking ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/AI-SEC-482 (creates checklists for metrics + circuit breaker).
Rachel (sec): Closing loop: priority is (1) schema + validation contract, (2) DEK caching plan with threat model, (3) backpressure + sampling. We'll re-evaluate after canary results.
